Plot methods for the package's objects

Source: R/plot.R
plot-methods.Rd

plot() on a rotation object shows the structure of the variance-covariance matrix of the adjusted means: the absolute correlations as an image in the order of the accessions (type = "correlation"), or the variances along the accessions (type = "variance").

On an efficiency object it shows the standard-error factor of inverse-variance weighting and of the unweighted analysis for every marker, against the minor allele frequency (type = "maf") or along the genome (type = "genome", which needs map).

On a genome_scan object it draws a Manhattan plot per scheme (type = "manhattan", positions from map or the marker order without one) with the Bonferroni threshold, the significant markers in red and the highlighted markers circled; or a QQ plot of the observed against the expected \(-\log_{10} p\) of every scheme in the object (type = "qq"), with the genomic inflation factors in the legend.

On a specification_test object it draws the profile of the REML deviance of the residual variance: the increase over its minimum as the residual variance moves, with the estimate, the target value one, the one-sided and two-sided critical values and the 90\

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rotation'
plot(x, type = c("correlation", "variance"), main = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'efficiency'
plot(x, type = c("maf", "genome"), map = NULL, main = NULL, xlab = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'genome_scan'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("manhattan", "qq"),
  map = NULL,
  scheme = NULL,
  highlight = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'specification_test'
plot(x, main = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

the object.

type

which plot, see the description.

main, xlab

titles; NULL gives the defaults described above.

...

further graphical parameters for the main plotting call.

map

optional data frame with the columns marker, chromosome and position (any unit), for the plots along the genome; the chromosomes are drawn in the order of their first appearance in map.

scheme

for the Manhattan plot, the scheme or schemes to draw, one panel each; by default every scheme in the object.

highlight

marker names to circle in the Manhattan plot.

Value

the data drawn, invisibly: the absolute correlation matrix or the variances; a data frame of the factors with their x coordinate; a data frame per scheme of the Manhattan coordinates, or a data frame per scheme of expected and observed \(-\log_{10} p\); the profile.

Examples

ex <- rotationGWAS:::toy_trial(n = 60, n_markers = 200, seed = 2)
r <- rotation(ex$means, ex$Omega, ex$relationship, ex$covariates)
plot(r)

plot(efficiency(r, ex$markers))

s <- genome_scan(r, ex$markers, scheme = c("rotated", "unweighted"))
plot(s, type = "qq")

plot(s, scheme = "rotated", highlight = ex$truth$causal)

plot(specification_test(r))
